title: Calendly Standard to self-hosted Cal.com
summary: Cal.com is a close feature match for Calendly, which makes this one of the cleaner swaps — if you have enough seats.

you_lose: Calendly's polish, particularly on mobile booking pages
Managed calendar-sync reliability — OAuth tokens to Google and Microsoft are now yours to keep alive
Some routing and workflow features gated behind Cal.com's own commercial licence
you_gain: Free seats, which is the whole argument once you pass a handful of users
Booking data in your own database

caveats: Cal.com self-hosted is a Next.js monorepo and is heavier to run than its feature list suggests. The 4 GB requirement is not padding.
Parts of Cal.com are under a commercial licence rather than the AGPL core. Check the /packages/features/ee directory against what you need before committing.
Google Calendar OAuth setup is fiddly and is the most common place this migration stalls.
